title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page continues Grothendieck's linearized (abelianized, GL(2,Ẑ)-level) analysis of the 'équation des lacets'. The unknowns are a pair of matrices α0 = (a b; c d) and f = (r s; t u) in GL(2,Ẑ). Both are ≡ 1 mod 2, i.e. they come by reduction from elements of π̂_{0,3}, the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus 3 points, whose abelianization is Ẑ^2 and which is tied to the principal congruence subgroup Γ(2). The constraints are det α0 = ε3 ∈ {±1}, det f = 1, and a twisting relation involving the order-3 automorphism ρ and the order-2 automorphism σ∞. The two binary quadratic forms that appear are c²+cd+d², the norm from Z[ω] (the elliptic point of order 3), and t²+u², the norm from Z[i] (the elliptic point of order 2).

Previous page. With c, d, t, u fixed and satisfying ε2(t²+u²) = ε3(c²+cd+d²), the unknowns a, b, r, s satisfy the affine-linear system (89): da − cb = ε3, ur − ts = 1, (c+d)a + db − ε2ε3(us+tr) = c²+cd+d². This system has rank 3, so its solutions form an affine line over Ẑ. The congruences force c ≡ 0 or 2 (4) and d ≡ ±1 (4), hence c²+cd+d² ≡ 1+c (4).

This page, step 1. Since t is even and u is odd, t²+u² ≡ 1 (4). So ε2 ≡ ε3(1+c) (4), i.e. ε2ε3 ≡ 1+c (4); this is (90). Thus c mod 4 together with det α0 = ε3 determines ε2.

Step 2: the lifting problem. Fix c, d, t, u satisfying (91): c ≡ t ≡ 0 (2), d ≡ u ≡ 1 (2), and c²+cd+d² = ε(t²+u²) ∈ Ẑ*, where ε := ε2ε3 is the sign with ε ≡ 1+c (4). The task is to find (a, b, r, s) solving (89) together with the congruences (92): b ≡ s ≡ 0 (2), a ≡ r ≡ 1 (2). This amounts to lifting the obvious mod-2 solution (a, b, r, s) ≡ (1, 0, 1, 0) to a Ẑ-solution.

Step 3: torsor reformulation. The solution set T is a torsor under Ẑ. Reducing mod 2 gives a quotient Z/2-torsor. The congruences select one element of that quotient, and its set of lifts is a torsor under 2Ẑ ≅ Ẑ. Grothendieck ends with 'Encore un mystère !', puzzled by where the factor 2 comes from.

Resolution (made explicit on the next page). The homogeneous system forces (a, b) = λ(c, d) and (r, s) = κ(t, u). The third equation then gives λ(c²+cd+d²) = εκ(t²+u²), so λ = κ. The direction of the line is therefore λ(c, d, t, u). Because d and u are odd, b and s change parity exactly when λ is odd, so the parity conditions cut out the coset λ ∈ 2Ẑ. This matches the action (α0, f) ↦ (l0^n α0, l0^n f), which shifts a, b, r, s by −2n·(c, d, t, u).
errors: No mathematical error. The 'mystery' of the 2Ẑ-torsor is elementary: the line's direction vector (c, d, t, u) has odd entries d and u, so parity is preserved exactly by even multiples. Grothendieck himself resolves this on the next page via the l0^n action.

ideas.what: Abelianized (GL2(Ẑ)) shadow of the loop equation. It forces a unit μ ∈ Ẑ* to be represented simultaneously by the norm forms t²+u² and c²+cd+d², with sign/congruence compatibility ε2ε3 ≡ 1+c mod 4.
ideas.modern_name: Linearized / abelianized Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type relations; image of GT or Gal(Q̄/Q) acting on the homology of the modular curve tower
ideas.where_published: Unpublished continuation of La Longue Marche (1981); not in the Esquisse in this form

ideas.what: Description of the solution set as a Ẑ-torsor, with parity conditions selecting a sub-torsor under 2Ẑ.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine mod-4 bookkeeping and a torsor reformulation within an exploratory computation. The 'mystery' is trivially explained and is explained by Grothendieck himself on the next page.
transcription_corrections: Top line: '+mod 4+' is added after 'c': 'la connaissance de c mod 4'.
In (91) the left side reads (c²+cd+d²) = ε(t²+u²) ∈ Ẑ*; the 'cd' does not appear struck in the image.

The torsor sentence should read roughly: 'cela signifie qu'on a donc un élément du Z/2Z-torseur quotient correspondant — l'ensemble de ses relèvements s'identifie à un torseur sous 2Ẑ ≃ Ẑ ... Encore un mystère !'
'on est amené à relever une solution déjà donnée mod 2 de ce système d'équations en une solution Ẑ-adique' is a plausible reading of the inserted 'Ẑ-'.
